name: Conquian
description: Conquian is widely regarded as the ancestor of all Rummy games, originating in Mexico in the 19th century. It is a 2-player draw-and-meld card game played with a 40-card Spanish deck (8s, 9s, and 10s removed from a French deck). Players take turns forcing the opponent to take offered cards or themselves draw from stock, building melds of 3+ in sequence or of a kind. The first player to meld their entire 10-card hand wins.

content.text: Conquian is widely regarded as the ancestor of all Rummy games, originating in Mexico in the 19th century. It is a 2-player draw-and-meld card game played with a 40-card Spanish deck (8s, 9s, and 10s removed from a French deck). Players take turns forcing the opponent to take offered cards or themselves draw from stock, building melds of 3+ in sequence or of a kind. The first player to meld their entire 10-card hand wins.

Believed to have originated in Mexico in the 1800s, possibly adapted from Chinese Mahjongg or from an earlier European game. It is considered the root ancestor of Gin Rummy, Oklahoma Gin, and all modern Rummy variants.
40 cards: Standard 52-card deck with 8s, 9s, and 10s removed. Rank order: A-2-3-4-5-6-7-J-Q-K.
10 cards each. Rest is stock. No initial discard pile.

items.text: Coon Can (American variant): American Southwest variant of Conquian. Played with full 52-card deck. Otherwise very similar mechanics.
